newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Blues the best Super 12 team - ACT coach.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Blues the best Super 12 team - ACT coach.

text.p: AUCKLAND, April 14 - With one of their major rivals in the Super 12 rugby competition consigned to the beaten list, the Auckland Blues are talking about lifting their game further against the Gauteng Lions on Saturday, NZPA reports.
The Blues thumped competition front runners the ACT Brumbies 41-29 at Pukekohe on Saturday then trumpeted a warning that they aim to add more firepower to their powerful all-round game.

The absence of Olo Brown, Robin Brooke and Richard Fromont from the awesome Blues pack was barely noticed by the fans as they displayed some fine handling skills with midfield backs Eroni Clarke and Lee Stensness making a major impact on the
game.

The defending Super 12 champions, by their own admission, hadn't played well all season but pushed that behind them with a vintage six-tries-to-four performance. It was only when they eased the pressure on ACT and had one man in the sinbin when ACT managed to score three quick tries. But by then the Blues were home and dry.
Coach Graham Henry and his captain Zinzan Brooke said that some serious soul-searching in the lead-up to game put their performance back on track.
"We played well and defended well but we've got some big games to come against Transvaal, Natal, New South Wales and Wellington," Henry said.
"We've got some top clashes so we need to go up in form from here."
Henry said although his team's commitment against the Brumbies had been pleasing, he would ask for more on Saturday at Eden Park.
"Transvaal have got a huge pack and they play very confrontational football," he said.
"They've also got a very good defensive backline, they're a bit like the South African side at the World Cup last time. They're going to be very hard to breach."
Brooke said last Saturday's performance came as a result of a poor game against Canterbury the previous weekend when Auckland squeaked home 29-28.

"There was a lot of soul searching through the week because of what happened to us against Canterbury. But sometimes having that happen can be good for you when you're going into a game like this," he said of the Brumbies game.
Brumbies coach Rod Macqueen, who was disappointed with his team's showing, was nevertheless gracious in defeat.
Having already played and lost to Transvaal and Natal away in South Africa, Macqueen said Auckland were the best side his team had faced.
"They are by far and away the best team we've played by a fair margin this year," the Brumbies coach said.
"If they play as well as they can and they are switched on they'll beat everyone in the competition.
"At times they seemed to have lacked a bit of urgency but I don't think it has anything to do with their talent or ability.
"They showed out there for about 60 minutes what they can do when they are switched on."
ACT will remain in Auckland until Thursday when they head down to Invercargill to play Otago while Auckland begin preparations for their game against the Gauteng Lions.
The Lions drew 16-16 against Northern Transvaal yesterday New Zealand time.
